quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight through your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Ride straight through your lane to cross angled railroad or trolley tracks. If you change your path angle, you may move into another lane and hit oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When carrying a load, where should it be secured?
questions.explanation: Secure loads as low as possible to keep your motorcycle balanced and stable.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright colors and reflective materials when riding, even in daylight.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the right side may encourage the passing driver to return to your lane too quickly.

questions.question: Is eye protection required for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Eye protection is required for all motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What feeling in your steering shows your front tire is flat?
questions.explanation: Heavy steering means your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What should you do with the front brake when making a U-turn?

options.text: Use both front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it may cause the bike to tip.
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it may cause the bike to tip.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn as it can cause the bike to tip over. Use only the rear brake to control your speed.

questions.question: What separates lanes moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean no passing. Dashed white lines mean passing is allowed if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns you that the right lane is ending ahead.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcycles pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, motorcycles should pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing before the next one begins.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light will change to red soon.
The light will change to green soon.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light will change to red soon.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal will turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, continue through.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Get closer to the vehicle ahead of you.
Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead of you.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Slow down and adjust your lane position as needed.

questions.question: A passenger should never:

options.text: Lean with the operator when turning.

questions.explanation: In South Carolina, passengers under 21 must wear a helmet and eye protection. It is recommended for all riders. Passengers should wear snug clothing to avoid catching on the motorcycle and should lean with the operator when turning. Passengers must never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: When your passenger gets on the motorcycle, tell them to:

options.text: Get on before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Tell passengers to stay quiet and still while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should get on only after the engine is started. They should sit as far forward as possible without bothering the operator.

questions.question: If you wear a jacket for protection in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take breaks often to cool down.
Remove the jacket to stay cool.

questions.explanation: A sturdy riding jacket protects you in a crash, no matter the weather. Jackets also protect you from dehydration in hot weather. Many motorcycle jackets are made to prevent overheating.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: The center of the lane has an oily strip. What should you know about it?

options.text: It is okay to ride on it unless it is raining.
Ride on it only if another vehicle is in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is okay to ride on it unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily center strip usually has enough grip for safe riding, except when wet. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side and stay in the center lane.

questions.question: To make a quick turn, you should:
questions.explanation: To make an evasive turn, get your motorcycle to lean quickly in the direction you want to go. The sharper the turn, the more the motorcycle must lean.

questions.question: When being passed, which part of your lane should you be in?
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by an oncoming vehicle, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing driver creates a dangerous situation for both of you.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Complete your pass within the posted speed limit. Only pass another vehicle where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: _________ of all collisions between a motorcycle and a passenger vehicle are caused by the driver failing to yield the right-of-way to the motorcyclist.
questions.explanation: More than half of collisions between motorcycles and passenger vehicles happen because drivers fail to yield the right-of-way to motorcyclists. Motorcyclists should never assume that drivers of larger vehicles will yield, even if they must by law.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front of you so you can use its lights to see the road ahead.
Keep riding at your normal speed to avoid being hit from behind.
Slow down and stay farther away from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther away from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and stay farther away from other vehicles. It is harder to see at night, so you need more time and space to react to dangers ahead.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should position your motorcycle:

options.text: On the outside of the curve.
On the inside of the curve.
Where you can safely handle the road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can safely handle the road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the road and traffic conditions, and adjust as needed.

questions.question: Before you start riding, you should make sure the fuel valve is:
questions.explanation: Before you ride, make sure the fuel valve is open. If it is closed, the engine may start with fuel left in the lines, but it will stop once that fuel runs out.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is usually most easily seen by other drivers when riding in which lane position?
questions.explanation: The center lane position is usually best when following a car because it puts you in the driver's rearview mirror. Always be ready to change positions if traffic or road conditions require it.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
You have limited escape route options.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have limited escape route options.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you time to react and room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When riding behind another vehicle, you should position yourself:

options.text: To be seen in the vehicle's side mirror.
To be seen in the vehicle's rearview mirror.
To be seen through the vehicle's passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: To be seen in the vehicle's rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When following a car, position yourself in the center of your lane behind it. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror, where drivers look much more often than at side mirrors.

questions.question: If you must carry a load on your motorcycle, it should be:

options.text: Carried on the gas tank in front of you.
Piled up against a sissy bar or frame on the back of the seat.

questions.explanation: Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on their motorcycle.

questions.question: Shifting gears up or down while in a curve:

options.text: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the curve.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in power to the rear wheel can cause a skid.
